{"text":"We are assessing claim CLM-0001 (loss on 14 March 2026). To progress the assessment, please reply once with the items below. Clarify the conflict between statements on file: The claimant asserts a sudden burst on the reported loss date, while the plumber reports significant corrosion at the joint and that the joint failed at the corroded section, indicating a gradual deterioration as the failure mechanism; both a sudden accidental burst and a failure due to long-term corrosion cannot both fully explain the cause of loss for coverage purposes.

Please provide: Evidence that the damage began at or immediately before the reported loss date (so that we can answer: Was the water damage sudden and accidental rather than gradual?)

Please provide: Technical evidence of when the leak or corrosion began (so that we can answer: When did the leak or damage begin?)

If an item is not available, please say so. A claims colleague will review your reply."}

{"text":"We are assessing claim CLM-0001 (loss on 14 March 2026). To progress the assessment, please reply once with the items below and attach any files you have. If an item does not exist, please say so. A claims colleague will review your reply.

- Provide any maintenance or inspection record for the kitchen supply pipe or the kitchen area showing entries and dates before the leak (who performed it and dates).
- Provide the date and time you first notified the insurer of this loss and any claim reference or the sent timestamp of that notification email.
- Upload a clear photograph showing the burst kitchen supply pipe/joint in place within the building fabric (e.g., in-wall or under-sink) including surrounding area for context.
- Provide the pipe installation invoice or the property plan that shows the kitchen supply pipe as a permanent fixed pipe/fitting within the building."}
